aria: Animated recap of the Grizzlies' 129 to 110 home win over the Nets: Cam Spencer's three at the halftime buzzer that made it 71 to 54, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Cedric Coward's 23 points and 12 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Grizzlies won in the paint and off turnovers, and the next game at Washington.
notes: Box score from the Grizzlies' 129–110 win over the Brooklyn Nets at FedExForum on Nov 14, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via WRAL), Field Level Media, The Commercial Appeal and Roundtable Sports (via Yahoo Sports). All 129 Memphis points and all 110 Brooklyn points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 71–54 Memphis at the half and 103–84 after three (Covers; Yahoo Sports; AP). Biggest leads: Memphis 26, Brooklyn 3 (Covers). Points off turnovers (30–15) are from The Commercial Appeal (via Yahoo Sports); bench points are added up from the Covers box score (Memphis 58, also reported by The Commercial Appeal; Brooklyn 32); the other team stats are Covers'. Records and ranks are from the site's standings (data/season.json) after Saturday's games: Memphis 9–4, sixth in the West; Brooklyn 3–9, 13th in the East.

Seven Grizzlies scored in double figures (AP): Cedric Coward 23 and 12 rebounds, Taylor Hendricks a career-high 22 off the bench (AP; Field Level Media), Javon Small 19, Cam Spencer 17 with 8 assists, Cameron Boozer 15, Isaiah Stewart 11 and Olivier-Maxence Prosper 11. Memphis snapped a four-game home losing streak, on the second night of a back-to-back (Field Level Media). Memphis was without Ty Jerome, Zach Edey and Jerami Grant; Brooklyn's Michael Porter Jr. was a late scratch for personal reasons (AP; The Commercial Appeal). Memphis is 6–0 on the road (Field Level Media, Nov 13; Saturday's game was at home) and plays at Washington (4–9, 12th in the East) on Monday at 7:00 PM ET (AP; site schedule); Washington hosts Houston on Sunday first (site schedule).

How it went: Memphis scored a season-high 38 in the first quarter, making 9 of 11 threes, and led by as many as 20 in the first half (AP; Field Level Media). Julius Randle's three with 5:12 left in the third cut it to 85–77; Memphis answered with a 16–1 run to lead 101–78 and was up 103–84 after three (Field Level Media; Roundtable Sports via Yahoo Sports). The lead reached 26 at 117–91 early in the fourth; Brooklyn got within 119–106 on a Danny Wolf three with 4:16 left (Field Level Media).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cam Spencer's three at the halftime buzzer, which made it 71–54 (AP: Spencer hit a 3-pointer at the buzzer to put Memphis up 71-54 at halftime; Roundtable Sports via Yahoo Sports). The move isn't described, so the shot is drawn as the template's plain pull-up three, and the clock on the board only marks the last second of the half. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Memphis Grizzlies or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Spencer's listed 6-foot-3 and 205 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-5 wingspan measured at the 2024 draft combine (Sportskeeda), in Memphis's home white with No. 24 (RealGM). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
